item.title: Trump to remove Rwanda and South Africa from US trade deal
item.description:
The News US President Donald Trump plans to remove South Africa and Rwanda from African Growth and Opportunity Act eligibility next year, stripping both countries of duty-free access to the US market under Washington’s flagship Africa trade program. Trump formally notified Congress and both governments of his decision, the Office of the US Trade Representative said Monday, after an annual review determined Pretoria and Kigali have been engaging in “concerning and pervasive” practices inconsistent with AGOA’s eligibility criteria. These include “barriers that undermine American trade and investment” and practices that “pose a threat to US national security and foreign policy interests in the region,” US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said. item.title: Full Court Denies DOJ Petition In California Election Case In About 7 Hours, No Reply Needed
item.description:
The U.S. Supreme Court ( SCOTUS ) on Monday rejected a Trump administration request to temporarily block lower-court rulings that denied requests to segregate more than 20,000 California mail-in ballots cast by people it says are likely not U.S. citizens. Justice Elena Kagan denied the appeal on the eve of the midterm elections without comment, and did not refer it to the other justices. The administration argued that the limited injunction would preserve the ballots while their eligibility is investigated, without canceling any votes. California and the federal government dispute whether the ballots are unlawful. "Once illegally cast ballots are counted and commingled with lawful votes, the resulting harm is impossible to remedy," the Department of Justice ( DOJ ) wrote in a court filing. item.title: Student protests resume in France as pupils return to school
item.description:
Jennie Shin is pleased to welcome Éric Fassin, Sociologist and Professor at Université Paris 8. “In a democracy, elections are very important, but it’s not the end of democracy. It’s the beginning,” explains Fassin. He interprets France’s student protest movement growing into a challenge to socioeconomic policy and what he describes as an “illiberal turn” in government. Connecting the treatment of working-class, racialized youth with wider restrictions on dissent, he argues that racism and democratic participation are central to understanding the unrest. His analysis also challenges the attribution of responsibility to the left, placing the government’s response within a broader debate over the normalization of oppressive measures and the far right.

item.title: Karl Bushby embraces his mother as he completes his 28-year walk around world
item.description:
“They say it takes a village. In this case, it took a world.” After 28 years and some 50,000 kilometres, British explorer and adventurer Karl Bushby has returned to his hometown of Hull, completing an extraordinary life journey across four continents that illustrates not only the limits of human endurance, but also the intricate relationship between individual determination, geopolitical constraints and a world of humanity. Speaking to France 24's François Picard shortly after his emotional homecoming, Bushby reflects on an undertaking that resembles a modern-day Odyssey, although the defining obstacles were often more geopolitical than mythological.

item.title: Judge accuses DOJ of 'weaponization,' tosses case against ex-FBI officials
item.description:
A federal judge tossed criminal charges against two former FBI officials accused of lying to Congress about the Hunter Biden investigation Monday, delivering a blistering rebuke of the prosecution and accusing the Trump administration's Justice Department of weaponizing the justice system. U.S. Magistrate Judge Zia Faruqui dismissed the criminal complaint against former FBI officials Nikki Cole Floris and Bradley Benavides from the bench, sharply criticizing the government's handling of the prosecution. "What has transpired here cannot be described as anything other than weaponization," Faruqui said, describing the case as a "rush job" directed by President Donald Trump and FBI Director Kash Patel.
